name: Hashrate re-arm under calm volatility — miner conviction in a low-vol-realized base
rationale: Trends that begin from a calm, low-realized-volatility base tend to be more orderly and persistent than those born in a high-vol whipsaw. The thesis pairs that volatility-regime filter with slow-capital confirmation: when btc_hashrate crosses UP (miners re-arm — structural conviction) AND realized volatility is BELOW a fitted ceiling (a calm base, not a chaotic spike) AND momentum is positive, we get a structurally-backed trend emerging from an orderly regime. Lower vol also means tighter, lower-turnover risk control — aligned with the low-fee bias. Go long spot. vol_realized is BOUNDED and gated by lt on its raw level; btc_hashrate is drifting and read ONLY via cross_up/cross_down. Exit when vol expands past an exit ceiling (regime breaks) or miners capitulate. Disconfirmer (core falsifier): the edge must come from miner re-commitment, not from the low-vol filter. If dropping the btc_hashrate cross_up arm (keeping vol_realized<ceiling + ret_Nd>0) matches or beats deflated Sharpe, hashrate is redundant and this is just a low-vol momentum trade. Low-confidence until OOS; the Gate decides.
catalyst: btc_hashrate crosses up while realized volatility is calm (below ceiling) and momentum is positive
